pass_a_gloss: If I-repaid to-the ones-repaying to-me evils, let-me-fall-away then from the enemies of-me empty. Empty is the not being-able to-say: From the fullness of-him we all received and grace instead-of grace. Wherefore also the such-ones reeds are-called, feeding in themselves the beasts, about which it-has-been-said: Rebuke for, he-says, the beasts of-the reed, and: The devil, says the Job, beside trees-of-every-kind he-sleeps, beside papyrus and rush and reed; this-one for king is of-all the-ones in the waters.
pass_b_english: “If I repaid those who repay me evils, then let me fall empty from my enemies” (Psalm 7:5).
Empty is the one who cannot say: “From his fullness we all received, and grace for grace” (John 1:16).

Therefore such people are also called reeds, feeding the beasts in themselves, about which it is said: “Rebuke the beasts of the reed” (Psalm 67:31); and: “The devil,” says Job, “sleeps beside trees of every kind, beside papyrus and rush and reed; for this one is king of all those in the waters” (Job 40:21; Job 41:26).

choices.why: Aorist optative of wish plus ἄρα. Not a counterfactual ‘I would fall’, and OCR α ρα is not αὐτά.
The empty man is the one who cannot say John 1:16. Contrast, not ‘vain’ or ‘fruitless’ as a moral tag.
rejected: unable to speak with no quote

choices.term: ἐκ τοῦ πληρώματος αὐτοῦ ἡμεῖς πάντες ἐλάβομεν
choices.english: from his fullness we all received
choices.why: αὐτοῦ is Christ’s fullness; ἐλάβομεν is receive, not fill. Exact John 1:16.
rejected: from their fullness we were filled

choices.english: rebuke the beasts of the reed
choices.why: ἐπιτιμάω = rebuke (Psalm 67:31 LXX). OCR καλά μου is καλάμου, not ‘my reed’. Not τιμή ‘honor’.
rejected: honor the beasts of my reed

choices.term: βασιλεύς ἐστι πάντων τῶν ἐν τοῖς ὕδασι
choices.english: king of all those in the waters
choices.why: Job 41:26 LXX of Leviathan, here the devil. ὕδασι = waters. Not woods (ὕλη) and not ‘lowest’.
rejected: lowest of all in the woods
